newsitem.title: UK: UK independent forecasts put yr-end rates at 7.25%.
newsitem.headline: UK independent forecasts put yr-end rates at 7.25%.

text.p: Official British interest rates will rise just one more time, to 7.25 percent, by the end of the year and will end 1998 at the same level, according to the latest summary of new independent forecasts, compiled by the Treasury.

A poll of 33 new forecasts by economists in the City and other institutions produced an average forecast of 7.31 percent for base rates in the last quarter of the year and 7.36 percent in the final three months of 1998.
Last month, the Treasury's survey of forecasts put base rates at 7.23 percent by the end of the year.
The Bank of England nudged up base rates to seven percent two weeks ago, the fourth quarter-point increase in as many months. But it said it would now pause to take stock of the economy.

The Treasury survey of forecasts forecast underlying inflation, excluding volatile mortgage payments, at 2.4 percent by Q4 1997, rising to three percent by late next year. The government has a target of 2.5 percent for RPIX.
